reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes an easy-income task application with claims of earning up to 6000-60000 rupees per month and directs viewers to register through the description link. The speaker presents an in-app balance and withdrawal process as evidence of earnings, then explicitly encourages unregistered viewers to sign up and start making money.

citations.quote: minimum withdrawal is 2000
you can start money making

opening.argument: The presentation is framed as an examination rather than an unconditional endorsement. The speaker expressly says the video will address whether the application is real or fake and says that “all these issues” will be covered. He also describes payment as dependent on reaching a threshold and on a stated payment window, which is uncertainty and procedure, not a guaranteed immediate return. The material therefore supports an investigation into the app’s claims, with viewers directed to consider the described rules, rather than proof that the creator deceptively certifies the service.

citations.quote: this application is real or fake all these issues are going to be covered in this video
minimum withdrawal is 2000
Next month 25th they will withdraw money which you earned during 25th till 5th

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution treats discussion of a registration link as conclusive solicitation, but the cited material does not show a guarantee of safety or payment. “You can start money making” describes the app’s intended activity; it does not establish that the presenter promises a particular outcome. The threshold and payment-window discussion instead communicates conditions viewers must understand.

citations.quote: Your money will be sent between the 25th and
you can start money making

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Calling something real-or-fake analysis does not neutralize the practical endorsement that follows. The speaker supplies the registration route and tells unregistered viewers they can begin making money. The threshold language also presents a claimed balance and a withdrawal pathway, but does not show an actual completed payment, so the cautionary framing does not overcome the promotional effect.

opening.argument: The video can be read as an operational walkthrough of an application’s stated process. It explains how to open the menu, reach payment details, enter a payment method, and understand the threshold and payment timing. The speaker also distinguishes the app’s stated rules from the question of whether it is real or fake. Showing a wallet balance and navigating payment screens is consistent with a tutorial or review demonstration; it does not by itself prove that the central purpose is deceptive recruitment.

citations.quote: You have to click payment, you have to come on payments details
You can fill your bank details, or and paytm or phone pin number
You can read their rules

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution’s description focuses on the existence of an earning balance and a signup instruction, but neither makes a screen-by-screen explanation a scam. The speaker spends substantial time explaining where payment details go and when payment is supposedly processed. Those are operational details that viewers could evaluate, not evidence that the demonstration hides a required payment or false outcome.

citations.quote: here they have to fill their payment details
The money you have sent It is sent between the 25th and 25th

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Operational detail can make a promotion more actionable; it does not make it neutral. The walkthrough ends by directing people who have not registered to use the description link and sign up. The displayed balance and payment screens show an interface, not independent evidence that earnings were generated or that withdrawal succeeded.

citations.quote: in the description box you will see a link to that link you will select and directly open its website
you can sign up from there and you can start money making

opening.argument: At most, the evidence shows promotion of an app and its referral-based signup process, comparable to an ordinary referral or rewards offer. The description supplies a referral code and signup URL, while the narration describes task earnings and payment options. Crucially, the supplied material does not show a deposit requirement, a guaranteed return, downline income, or a completed payment. It describes filling bank, Paytm, or PhonePe details, but that is not itself evidence of a scam mechanism. The category should not certify the external service as safe merely because it is promoted, but promotion alone does not establish scam content.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution infers a scam from task-based earning and a referral link, but those features also occur in ordinary rewards and referral promotions. Its cited threshold screen shows an in-app condition, not a deposit, guaranteed return, or downline structure. The record likewise does not establish that the presenter asks viewers to surrender money or that any promised payment failed.

citations.quote: minimum withdrawal is 2000
Koo taka referral Code: - T3B27453

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The referral code and signup URL make the content actionable recruitment, not merely neutral observation. The app is presented as a way to earn from tasks, with a displayed balance and a stated withdrawal route. Although the supplied record does not show a deposit, a deposit is not required for this low-barrier reward-acquisition pattern; the missing proof of successful payment reinforces that the earning claim is unverified.
